answers.children: Treeing Walker Coonhounds are moderately good with children thanks to their friendly and sociable nature. Their energetic build and determined hunting background mean they can be boisterous around small children and may knock them over during play. Owners must provide plenty of structured activity so the hound’s high energy does not overwhelm a household with kids.
answers.other-pets: Treeing Walker Coonhounds get along well with other dogs because of their sociable temperament yet their strong prey drive often leads them to chase smaller animals. Bred specifically to track and tree raccoons, they view cats and pocket pets as quarry. A secure environment and careful introductions are essential to prevent pursuit behaviour indoors and out.
answers.exercise: Treeing Walker Coonhounds need at least two hours of vigorous daily exercise. Long hikes, scent work and simulated hunting trails suit their stamina and tracking instincts; without this they become restless and destructive. Their boundless energy, developed for covering vast wooded terrain, quickly turns to pacing or chewed furniture in under-stimulated homes.
answers.shedding: Yes — Treeing Walker Coonhounds shed moderately year-round. Their short smooth single coat produces fine hair that clings to furniture and clothing yet requires minimal removal effort. The lack of feathering or undercoat means shedding stays even rather than dramatic, though weekly wiping still helps control the loose hairs scattered through the house.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Treeing Walker Coonhound is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short smooth coat still releases dander and seasonal hair that can trigger reactions. The breed’s hunting heritage leaves it with a functional coat that sheds enough to make strict allergy management necessary.
answers.training: Treeing Walker Coonhounds are not easy to train because of their independent streak and focus on scent over commands. Bred to hunt without constant human direction, they show moderate trainability and can ignore cues when a trail interests them. Patience and scent-based games help channel their intelligence into acceptable behaviour at home.
answers.lifespan: Treeing Walker Coonhounds live 12-14 years. Their medium build and robust health support an active life well into the later years when given appropriate exercise and mental work. The breed’s history of stamina for long hunts contributes to a sturdy frame that holds up provided energy needs continue to be met.
answers.size: Treeing Walker Coonhounds reach 50-70 lb and stand 20-27 in at the shoulder. Their lean, athletic proportions give them a rangy feel that takes up moderate space yet requires room to move. Living with this size means a sturdy dog that can lean affectionately but also needs a yard or regular outings to match its hunting heritage.
answers.barking: Treeing Walker Coonhounds bark a lot, especially their melodic bay when they detect scent or movement. Bred to tree raccoons and alert hunters with loud vocalisation, they announce everything from passing cats to boredom. The frequent sound carries far and can disturb neighbours or wake households at night.
answers.apartment: Treeing Walker Coonhounds do not suit apartment living well. Their high energy and loud baying, developed for tracking through forests, make them restless and vocal indoors without constant activity. Even with exercise the breed’s determined nature and need for purposeful work mean they struggle to settle quietly in small confined spaces.
answers.first-time: Treeing Walker Coonhounds are not a good first dog because their high energy and independent hunting drive demand experienced handling. The combination of strong prey drive, frequent baying and need for two hours of targeted exercise can overwhelm novices. Their friendly affection is rewarding only after an owner learns to meet the breed’s substantial mental and physical requirements.
